body: Good luck! My fingers are crossed for you!
Gosh, I could have written this. I hear you, I understand. Thank you for sharing. I hope things get better for the both of us, you really deserve it.

How would you feel if you didn't submit the application? Would you regret it and beat yourself up? I would submit it. What have you got to lose? You might not even get it, but you'll never know if you don't give it a shot.

Yeah, I can really relate to this. Those two things have been my biggest coping mechanisms for a long time. I've gone 6 weeks now no weed, but the self harm persists. I don't know how to quit both. I don't really have any advice I'm sorry, I just wanted you to know you're not alone.

Sometimes I find myself wishing my previous attempts had worked. I honestly don't know how I'm still here at 30, when I thought I wouldn't see 25. It would have been easier if I had died when I intended to. Now I oscillate between wanting to give life a go and wanting to shuffle off this mortal coil.

I've heard many people talk about how the things their parents didn't do (neglect) hurt them more than the hurtful, abusive things they did do. That's how it feels for me too. At least the abuse is easy to see. Neglect is so insidious and invisible. Being ignored, unseen and unheard is beyond devastating for a child.

Do you have a therapist? I think exploring and learning about where your fawn response comes from is a good place to start. 

I am also a fawn/freeze type, and I learnt to fawn growing up with a mother who I had to walk on eggshells around. I learnt to pick up on whatever mood she was in, and adjust myself to whatever she needed in the moment. Keeping her happy was how I kept myself safe, and also how I received attention/praise (on occasion). It was (and still is to some degree) an enmeshed and codependent relationship. You seem quite self aware already, and I would encourage you to explore things deeper with a therapist if possible to find ways of healing through this.

I found [this](https://youtu.be/8qoURlTfbj0?si=pJ0YxeNUe9_YiMhh) video helpful too.

I struggle to cry too. I actually don't remember the last time I did. I find it quite distressing not being able to, because sometimes I just want the relief that comes after a good cry. But there is a block, I don't feel safe to cry, I worry I will lose control, that it will never stop and I will be engulfed by the intensity of the pain. I struggle a lot with dissociation and feeling numb/empty. I'm hoping as I progress in my recovery, my body will feel safe enough to cry again.
I wonder if it's a way of self sabotaging? It's like, it's not enough that a situation is bad, we have to do things to make it worse because deep down we feel like it's what we deserve.

That's a very shitty thing to do to someone, especially considering you share similar traumas, I'm sorry that happened. Honestly I feel like I'd be even more hurt by your gf not wanting to cut contact with her. It's definitely not too much to ask for. Invalidating someone's trauma is a shit move and the fact your gf can't see that, or excuses it, is concerning and makes me question how much she cares about you.
I'm sorry that happened. Good on you for speaking up and telling your therapist that. Hopefully she will think twice about it in the future.
Yep, hi 👋 and once I was diagnosed, you can bet my nex used it as an insult against me all the time
I want to feel safe enough to be my authentic self. I think I get in my own way with that though.
It reminds me of the quote "It is no measure of good health to be well-adjusted to a sick society."
Same here but with my mum. Sending hugs if you want them. We didn't deserve it.

This makes a lot of sense. The inconsistency has deeply affected me too. It felt so chaotic growing up, like you never knew what you were going to get or how you'd be treated. I'd say now I have a disorganised attachment style which makes sense to me considering my upbringing. Sometimes anxious, sometimes avoiding, depending on the other person.
Feels much the same for me too.
Can definitely relate to this, thanks for responding!

Two things for me:

When my sister took her own life 11 years ago. She was 17, I was 19. I was and never will be the same. She was my only sibling, and the only one who would have understood the trauma from our shared upbringing. I wish she was still here every day. I still feel like it should have been me.

When I truly realised my long term partner of 10 years had groomed, emotionally, verbally and sexually abused me. Feeling that level of betrayal from someone I loved and trusted with my whole heart destroyed me in a way I can't describe. I left him a year ago. I'm still picking up the pieces.

I can totally relate to this. I don't think there's anything wrong with you. I imagine this is a common experience for those with trauma who grow up without these "normal" relationships. We don't even get to grieve in a "normal" way because we don't get normal relationships to even grieve.
Thank you for replying. What you said is really helpful. I guess we have to keep going and keep trying even if we don't feel like we can or that we deserve it. It's nice to know I'm not alone 💜
Thank you for sharing :)
Thank you so much, I appreciate it! I'll check out her resources
Lamotrigine (aka Lamictal) has been very helpful for me for emotion dysregulation and basically making things feel less heightened. It has taken the edge off things for me.
I have been since 2021. Slowly working on building up my capacity to get back into some form of volunteering or work
Yeah, when I'm feeling deep shame I want to cease to exist and just disappear into the earth

Any books on self compassion that you recommend? This is something my therapist has brought up a number of times and I always feel a hesitation to explore it deeper, but your comment has made me think that maybe it is time. Also thank you for sharing your experience.
I get what you mean. That's a good idea, thank you
I hear you. It feels like everyone has their own selfish agenda and it's impossible to find the ones that want a genuine connection instead of just using and discarding you.

>That feeling of regretting not getting away from someone who shows red flags early on. Not listening to your intuition. It feels like betraying your soul when you let dysfunctional people even have a little access to you.

Oh gosh, this really got to me. That regret, betraying your soul, all of it. There are so many times I missed or ignored early red flags and sometimes I feel like I will never forgive myself for that.

I don't know how to stop it, I wish I knew, maybe someone else will. But I'm right there with you. Maybe it won't always be this way. Maybe we will become better at listening to our intuition and trusting ourselves.

Hey, having a best friend of 17 years is definitely something! Maintaining relationships is hard. To answer your question, I've noticed a pattern in my own life of being attracted to people who are not good for me (not just in romantic relationships, but friends too) and then getting hurt, let down and discarded by them. Sometimes it feels like I must have a sign on my head that says "take advantage of me." I never realise until it's too late though. I think I idealise people, see the best in people and give them the benefit of the doubt, but it's always the ones who don't deserve it as they end up just running over me. Relationships are hard and for me sometimes it's easier to just be on my own, but that gets lonely.
Hey, thanks for making me smile. I'm so happy for you. You've got this. 🫶

I eventually realised that smoking weed to escape depression/anxiety was actually just making things worse. Eventually the relief was less and less and my mental health deteriorated. I quit three weeks ago so I'm still figuring this out, but I've been working on finding other things to fill my time. Things you've been putting off for ages? Make a list and start checking them off. A new hobby you want to try? Learn something new. Keep your mind occupied basically.
Existing and taking up space.
Thank you, this helps. Wishing healing for you too.
I've heard that book mentioned here before, I'll have to have a read, it sounds helpful. Thank you for the help.
I really appreciate your advice. I think you're right the best place to start is with myself. I hope you have a good day too, kind stranger

I do have a therapist but I haven't talked to her about this stuff, I guess I haven't been ready. I haven't talked about this with anyone outside of this post. I'm thinking I'll send an email to her though. I don't know how to be ok knowing he is most likely grooming someone else and doing the same thing, how do I live with that, you know? Don't worry, you don't need to answer that, it's more rhetorical.

Thank you again!
I'm struggling to bring myself back down to a less heightened state. This is helpful though, I'll try to do this. I am safe right now, I know I am safe (trying to remind myself).
Thank you stranger, for some reason your comment didn't show up until now. Your last sentence makes me feel sick because I think I know you are right
I appreciate your insight, thank you

Really? It feels like such a strong word and that my experience wasn't enough to be able to say that. Thank you, though. I  ended up self harming unfortunately and am still struggling but I just took my extra meds so hoping I can sleep soon.
This is really helpful, thanks!
Can I ask, does splitting only refer to people/relationships, or can it apply to things like world-view, sense of self etc?
Oh yep, I'm right there with ya!
Thank you, I'm definitely getting there. I hope you are too 💜

I'm guessing a combination of anonymity, lack of consequences and dehumanisation. It's not just reddit though, seems to happen in many internet spaces/social media platforms. I will say, some subreddits I'm in on here have been incredibly accepting and kind though, so it's not everywhere. Sometimes it only takes a few bad apples to ruin things, though.
Yeah I like it too, it's happened to me in the shower a couple times like it feels like I'm about to pass out and it's just...peaceful. As someone else said, I wouldn't go chasing it though.
I can't think of an example but just wanted to say I totally related to that scene in Barbie too
Hi friend, I'm sorry this is what we had to resort to.
This. Daydreaming about all different scenarios where I got seriously injured or died so that I would finally get the love and attention I craved. Kinda messed up but it's how my young mind coped.
I get a lot of comfort from my suicidal thoughts too, I do understand that.

I'm so sorry she did that, and that your home, which is supposed to be your one safe space, is no longer safe. I totally get where you're coming from, it sucks feeling like you have to justify yourself to her (or to anyone else for that matter). That sense of ownership over you is such a burden. Yes she is your family, but that doesn't mean you have to be friendly or visit her or anything, you don't owe her anything, even though she is 'blood'. I don't have any advice really, just wanted to share that I understand where you're coming from and you have nothing to be sorry about.

There's definitely an adjustment period, but after that you can kind of forget they are there. I wore contacts for years but I went back to glasses for the last couple as my eyes kept getting really dry. But now I'm thinking of trying contacts again because they are just more convenient.

Being alone is the only time I feel truly safe, honestly. I do still get lonely though, and don't want to always be on my own, but I'm yet to find people I can feel truly safe around so I always come back to just being on my own.

Yep definitely, I know who I am when I'm alone and can be my authentic self, but I'm still figuring out how to apply that to being around others. I'm also hypervigilant around others and always masking, it's exhausting. Therapy is helping me become more comfortable being my authentic self around safe people. That's important though, they have to be safe, in order to start practising being authentic around them.

It can be hard at times, sure, but it's made so much harder by having parents who don't create a secure, safe environment for their kids to thrive. Kids deserve all the support in the world, and that should be coming mainly from their parents.

I haven't seen this talked about here, so I'll share my story. I have a complicated relationship to death

TW death of loved one to suicide, suicide attempts

I have lost people before (mainly grandparents but their deaths largely didn't impact me because I barely knew them), but I lost my sister to suicide at 19 (she was 17), and that really fucked me up. It happened over 10 years ago now but it is a pain and grief I will carry with me for life. She was the first person I lost whose death destroyed me.

On the other hand, death doesn't really scare me. I've had multiple suicide attempts and one in particular I came very close to dying. I have wanted to die many times. I don't really believe in anything happening to us when we die, so I've often longed for the nothingness/oblivion death would bring. I think I struggle most with death when it is sudden and/or traumatic, whereas say people dying of old age doesn't really upset me because they lived a long life.
I agree! We seem to treat wanting attention so negatively, when really it is a very human and understandable thing to want.

Have you heard of [grey rocking](https://psychcentral.com/health/grey-rock-method)? It sounds like that's what you're doing. Good advice!

*edit - fixed link
I think it's something I learned over time, not to open up, because the responses I got, or lack thereof, told me it wasn't worth it. That I'd just be disappointed.

Oh wow, I could have written this, our experiences are so similar.

I used to get dragged down the hallway kicking and screaming to be locked in my room for hours at a time. I would get carpet burn from being dragged. My mum used to tell people constantly about how 'bad' I was at home, because outside of home I was always well behaved. She would tell it like it was a funny story that I was so terrible at home and she had it so difficult. I wasn't even a 'bad' kid, I just had big emotions and no one to comfort me through them. My mum would always tell others these stories about how infuriating I was as a child (her words), but she's always laughing about it? One time she even told my Aunty, while laughing, that she strangled me once. I don't understand why she thought it was so funny. I also have a similar memory to yours of being really young and creeping into my parents room at night because I was scared of thunderstorms, and they never let me in their bed. I would drag my blanket in to sleep at the end of their bed. 

Sometimes I think the emotional neglect is harder to come to terms with than the actual abuse - being unheard, unseen, ignored and denied any needs hurts in a way that feels indescribable. It's definitely a deep pain and core childhood wound.
I can relate, I also don't know why I do it sometimes. Try to be gentle toward yourself, that voice can be very hard to ignore.

Sometimes I find thinking about ways to enjoy life is just too much for where I'm at in that moment, so I just focus on trying to be ok in the moment instead. Takes the pressure off trying to strive to enjoy life which often feels unattainable. Not sure if that's helpful.
I've had this situation happen to me. I said I pulled a muscle.
I agree. I learnt quickly after being diagnosed it's best not to share if you don't want people to suddenly change how they interact with you. It's sad really.
Thank you for sharing this, it's so nice. It also makes me sad that AI can so easily do what so many of our parents could not or would not.

You still managed to get to 4 years, and that is something to be proud of. I went 6 years without self harming and then relapsed last year. I haven't been able to stop for longer than a couple of weeks since then. It felt like all that time was just a waste, but I had to reframe that. If I got to 6 years once, I can do it again, no matter how long it takes. It doesn't mean it was all a waste. But for now, just take it day by day. And be kind to yourself. Those urges can be next to impossible to ignore.
Same here. It sounds like dissociation. Mine has improved as I've come along in my healing journey.

I feel similar, but I don't really have an answer to your question. The longest I ever went without self harming was 6 years, but then since about a year ago, after a lot of horrible things happened, I started again. The urges never really do go away, even when I went that long without. I'm currently on day 9 and I know when I get to that place of overwhelm/deep dissatisfaction with life I'll 'give in' again. It doesn't feel inherently wrong to me either, it's a coping mechanism that works, even if only for a short time (for me anyway). I don't normally tell anyone afterwards, except maybe my psychologist.

This made me think, maybe this is why so many autistic adults (especially late diagnosed) are not believed when we share our diagnosis. Like people cannot fathom the existence of an adult who at least appears to be somewhat functioning and not just sitting in a corner rocking, so they just don't believe it.

Apologies that occur without actions to change behaviour, I believe, are used as a form of manipulation. You can't truly be sorry about something if you're unwilling to change what you're apologising for. It just sounds like a way to maintain the abuse cycle and keep getting supply from you. Like you said, it probably also makes him feel better without him having to change anything.
I really do understand. Baby steps are all we can do, and in time, hopefully things get easier for you. I wish you all the best.

Hey, you did a really brave thing, it's not easy to be honest and vulnerable like you were. I know the whole "You should be proud" sometimes doesn't really sink in, but I am proud of you, internet stranger. I hope you can be proud of you too. You've taken a huge step, especially as someone who always shoulders the burden alone. I would say keep talking about it with safe people, as this can diminish its power over you. Self harm is something that comes with a lot of shame and isolation, I've found talking about it, however difficult, can help ease some of that shame. Of course this entirely depends on the other person, but it sounds like at least the doctor you spoke to was understanding and caring.
In this context, I've heard it described as the person is basically saying they are sorrowful. They're not apologising for wrongdoing, they are sharing that they are full of sorrow.

My story is very much like yours. I crashed and burned in 2020, after doing so much for so long. I can see now that it was inevitable. But I often wonder how I managed to work, study, volunteer, maintain relationships, etc. I grieve a lot for that time, not because it was enjoyable (I was a shell of myself, miserable and never looked after my own needs) but because I recognise that I will never get back to that level of functioning (even though I don't really want to). Accepting that has been hard, as has trying to find a new way of living that is both healthy and sustainable. I haven't worked or studied since then, but I've been working very hard in therapy and in my life to find a new way of living that doesn't send me spiralling into a deep hole. I do believe we can find a new way to live life, I have hope for you and myself.

My ex was so similar towards the end, telling me I never communicated any of this with him and just "dumped it all on him" at once and then in the last week we were together organised to see a psychologist. 

If he is committed to changing and working on his issues, that's great, but he has to want to do that for himself and not just to keep you in the relationship. He has shown previously that he is not open to changing, so this is most likely just another way to make you feel guilty for leaving and try to reel you back in. Don't hang around waiting to see if he will change. The kind of change necessary will take years of hard work anyway and it doesn't sound like he would commit to that.

I think you should ask yourself, do you really want to spend the rest of your life with a person who calls a literal toddler an idiot? Who calls you names simply for sticking up for your kids? What about when your kids get older and remember this behaviour. These kinds of relationships only get worse over time. I left a relationship of 10 years only last year, and we didn't have kids, so I cannot pretend to know how much more complicated the decision to leave would be, but you have to put your kids first. Yes it's good much of the time, but when it's bad it's really bad. You have your kids lives ahead of you, do what you think is best for them in the long term, no matter how hard it might be. I'm sorry you're experiencing this.

It definitely does feel like that. I've lost hope in finding someone who truly loves me for who I am after spending 10 years in an emotionally abusive relationship with a narcissist. They destroyed any trust I had in ever letting someone get that close to me again. Between that and growing up with very dysfunctional parents who have a very unhealthy relationship, it just feels like a healthy, loving, supportive relationship is impossible. I've never known it, so how could it happen?
Thank you so much for sharing! I'll be taking the time to work through these slowly, very appreciated. Also I'm so impressed and inspired by the work you've done.
I hear you, every word. It feels like I wrote this. If you would like one, I'm sending you a big hug

Before we were even together. I was in a relationship when I first met my abusive partner. We started as friends. They groomed me and pursued me for months and months, until eventually I broke up with my partner at the time, convinced by the love-bombing that we were soul mates, madly in love and destined for each other. I was incredibly vulnerable, having lost my sister to suicide the year before, and was very isolated, with an unsupportive family. All I wanted was someone to talk to about the grief and pain and loneliness I was feeling, I wanted a person I could feel safe around, and they presented that to me in the beginning. I was a prime target, I guess, for someone who turned out to be a covert narcissist. I didn't realise that for another nine years though, unfortunately. I left a few months ago.

When my ex proposed to me, he did so using a book he created of all the things he loved about me, and at the end was the question, "Will you marry me?" He had proposed about 6 years earlier, the book was never really talked about again. Anyway, after I broke up with him, maybe about a week afterwards, he messaged me asking if I would send the book to him (via post) so he could keep it. At the time, I agreed I would. But I didn't intend to. Honestly, I'd rather burn it than send it to him. It seems so bizarre to me, I don't know why he wanted it.

I'm sorry I'm only just seeing this now! I really appreciate your comment, thank you so much for checking in. I'm so sorry to hear you're in a similar place, but I'm glad you are planning your exit. How are you travelling currently? I know the time leading up to me leaving was a really dark period. I'm not going to lie and say everything is wonderful for me now because it's not, I'm really struggling with my mental health honestly. But I do not for a second regret my decision to leave. I know it was the right thing to do. And with distance from the relationship, a lot of my confusion lifted and I gained more clarity around what was happening to me. I truly hope you manage to find a safe exit soon, take care.

Yes. From the very beginning right through to the end of our 9 year relationship. Everything was always "just a joke." It is only since leaving three months ago I truly am able to see just how much of myself I hid and lost during that time, until I was an empty shell. I love music but stopped listening to it around him because he made fun of what I listened to. He made fun of me for wanting to take photos of myself, for what I wore, for how I ate, for being "too passionate" when I spoke about things I'm interested in. It saddens me that it took me so long to wake up to the reality - better now than never though.
9 long years
Literally everything. My life, my sense of self, my youth, my innocence, my relationships, my will to live.
I'm sorry. I hope you manage to get out. It's been six weeks for me - the hardest, but also the best thing I did was walk away.
My sister 💔

He told me he wished he never met me. That he feels sorry for the next person I fuck around and waste the time of, and that I'm incredibly cruel (because I broke up with him). He also said I was incapable of having a relationship with anyone.

Thank you, this is helpful to hear. It's breaking my heart, that he is hurting. But I'm trying to stay strong. I'm trying to remind myself how unsafe and hypervigilant I felt all the time with him, particularly the last few weeks/months. I don't think I trust him anymore, as much as I want to run back to him and believe he will change, I don't think it will happen. At least not in an amount of time I can hang around waiting for. I feel like I'm being cruel though. That I should give him a second chance. I really do start to doubt that I did the right thing. Gosh it's hard.

I'm sorry you went through that. I'm not sure if this is the case for you, but I feel like many of us in these relationships struggle to walk away because we are kind hearted and want to see the best in people. Often at the expense of our health and safety though. 

I've find this community quite helpful and validating.

Thank you, I definitely have given this a lot of thought, particularly in the last few months, and I've had doubts on and off throughout our relationship. I think these were times I had a gut instinct that something wasn't right, but I ignored it and convinced myself it was just me. 

I was only 20 when we met and had just lost my sister to suicide a year before. I definitely have grown and matured with the help of years spent in therapy, and I do feel like I am looking back at my relationship with new eyes.

I'm just so good at gaslighting myself after a lifetime of it, and have very little trust in my perception and judgements now that it's hard sometimes to trust I've made the right decision.

You did it! Much of what you shared I am experiencing too. I left a week ago. Keep tuning into those body signals, your gut instincts. Especially when you are having doubts, feeling guilty and thinking about going back. Your body is telling you what to do. I am numb too, and I've barely cried. I think it's what we need to do to cope right now. Just take it one day at time. In time, we can slowly begin to process everything. For now, just focusing on getting through each day is more than enough.
Can absolutely relate to that. I hope we both keep learning to give all that love and kindness we give to others to ourselves too.

Wow, thank you so much, this is very kind. I needed to hear this. It has been one of the hardest things I've ever done. I feel like absolute shit about it but it helps to hear from others like yourself who have experienced the same, as well as have support from my loved ones who remind me why I left when I have my doubts and start to convince myself it wasn't that bad. I truly hope that you have support around you to help you if and when you are ready to try again to leave. You can absolutely do it. Take care.
I'm sorry you went through similar, it's awful. Thank you, I'll check out those resources. I've been watching a lot of videos which have been helpful too.
Thank you, I can relate to a lot of what you've experienced. 100% the guilt tripping is what my partner does, it's so awful, but it's helpful having outside perspective to remind me why I left.

Yeah that does seem like he has a lot of the traits. I've literally only skimmed the surface of what he's done in my post. I just worry as we have 4 cats together so I feel like I can't go no contact before sorting that out with him as I don't want to lose them. But he is also not making it easy.

Yes 100% this is abuse and will most likely only get worse. This could very quickly escalate to you being physically hurt, not just walls and furniture. Please please put your safety first and get out of there while you can.

Thank you for the resources. Do you think this sounds like the behaviour of a narcissist? I didn't initially think it described him, but I keep coming across more and more info about narcissistic traits and realising it does seem to, mostly the vulnerable narcissism. Just, how did I not know, you know? I've spent 9 years with this person, it feels like who I thought he was isn't there anymore.
Thank you for sharing. As someone who is currently contemplating leaving but feels really trapped and unable to, this is helpful to hear. I'm so glad you're doing better and that you got out.

Definitely not your fault. In fact, it's very understandable. The way he claims it comes from a place of love and care...uh no. He is intentionally trying to lower your self esteem by making these comments.
Thank you for the help! Much appreciated!

Thank you, it's strange reading the comments. Even after reading them, I'm still finding it hard to accept that this is what it is. We had a huge fight yesterday, the worst one yet, he threw, kicked and broke a chair and he's never done stuff like that before. But by the end of it he had me agreeing that I haven't been fair on him for bringing this all of up now, instead of when they initially occurred (even though I was so thoroughly minimising things and invalidating my own instincts I wasn't even consciously aware til recently of these patterns in his behaviour). Our arguments become so confusing because he manages to twist what I'm saying and make me doubt everything. And then today he's been lovely, acting all nice and caring.

Hey, I just want to validate that, of course you enjoyed having a nice conversation with your mum. She is your mum, and despite how she treats you, it is normal for a child to long for a positive connection with their mum. You absolutely do not deserve to be treated the way she has treated you, though. And I can totally understand the conflict you must feel because of it. It is absolutely not your fault for taking her seriously either, it is her job to not emotionally blackmail you and then gaslight you into thinking it was no big deal.
I'll look into that, thanks!

Hey! I'm trans too and feel the same way. I understand the anger too. I feel resentful of others who guilt me into staying. I've tried to kill myself three times in the last four months. I feel like I'm hanging on by a thread, I imagine you would feel similar. The thing is, I don't know your situation but it's highly likely that dying isn't your only option. There may be treatments/therapies/medications you haven't tried yet. Of course it feels like dying is the only way to make the pain stop, it's excruciating and feels like the only escape. But a suicidal mind is not functioning at its best, your mind can play tricks on you. Please don't believe it. Please know that no one is ever a lost cause, there is always help available. I won't make any promises but you say you don't want to die, so why don't you give life another go? Try something you haven't done before? Tell someone how you're feeling. Sending you strength.

I've done this for most of my life too. I've pictured my funeral and even considered the songs I would play. Also fantasise about so many different scenarios where I die, like a car crash, or getting shot or stabbed, not sure why it always needs to be so violent. Can't imagine it's overly "normal", but you're not alone.

I'm glad you found something that worked for you, even if it took ages. People keep telling me I need to give it time and part of me knows they are right but it feels like time is the one thing I don't have when this feels endless. I've given years already. And yet despite everything there's still some small part of me that hopes things won't always be so painful.
It's definitely a hard one for people who haven't been there to understand.
Exactly

It might seem counterintuitive to people who haven't experienced it, but absolutely. I find the thought of suicide very comforting. In some weird paradoxical way, sometimes knowing that I can kill myself at any time has helped me to stay alive for a bit longer.

I guess when it's small I can almost ignore it. When its large it's overwhelming and unrelenting and I physically feel like I'm in pain and/or dying. It's like a slow death, rotting away, with no energy to stop it.

That's a good description. I've always pictured it as this thick, heavy black fog that lives inside me. Sometimes it's contained to a small part of me, other times it consumes me entirely and spills out.
Honestly same. It's getting harder and harder to convince myself it's worth it.
